Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Built two real things this round:

**Fixed a bug in `lib/flip.ts`** (my file, not new scope): read through Claude A's actual `Leaderboard.tsx` integration and found the FLIP math was wrong — the list renders `flex flex-col gap-sm` (12px flex gap between cards), but `computeFlipDiff`'s cumulative-offset sum only counted each card's own `getBoundingClientRect().height`, never the gap between them. Every deltaY was understated by `(positions moved × 12px)`, compounding on a big rank jump (a #20→#1 move would've landed ~228px short of its real slot — a visible misalignment, not just a rounding error). Added a `gapPx` option defaulting to 12 (matching `--spacing-sm`/`gap-sm`), so Leaderboard's existing call — which doesn't pass it — now gets correct behavior automatically, no other file needed changes. Updated `tests/lib/flip.test.ts` with an explicit gap-accounting test and isolated the old height-only tests with `gapPx: 0`. Also confirmed by hand that reusing post-render measured heights for both prev/next cumulative offsets is actually sound here (offer content is immutable once created, so a card's height doesn't change between renders) — that part of Claude A's wiring is correct, not a bug.

**Added `tests/lib/contrast.test.ts`** — closes [REDACTED:high_entropy], which three phases promised ("verified in both modes") without anyone naming the mechanism. It parses the real hex values straight out of `app/globals.css` (no hand-copied palette to drift out of sync), computes WCAG relative luminance/contrast ratios, and asserts against the actual pairings components use — ink/ink-secondary on background+surface at 4.5:1, `danger` on `surface` at 4.5:1 (matching exactly how Leaderboard's error alert renders it), `success` on background at the 3:1 large-text/UI floor since nothing renders it as body text yet. I hand-computed every ratio (smallest margin: success-light at 4.02 vs its 3:1 floor, everything else ≥5:1) since `npm install`/`vitest` are still approval-gated in this sandbox for me too — same wall the integrator hit, confirmed not just inherited.

**Left for the group:** I still can't execute `npm install`/`vitest run` here, so these fixes are hand-verified, not machine-verified — that's the same real gap the integrator flagged, still open. One UX nit for Claude A, not a bug, not touching their file: `Leaderboard`'s aria-live announcement always narrates `offers.find(isOwnSubmission) ?? offers[0]`, so on an ambient-poll reorder where #1 didn't move but something lower did, it'll announce "#1 moved to 1st place" when #1 didn't actually move — worth a look whenever that file's back in rotation, not urgent.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
